title: Counterparty notes — risk storyboard and negotiation cues
content:
Personal scratchpad: quick, tactical notes for negotiating clauses that frequently create pushback with customers and partners. Purpose: make predictable trade-offs and have ready language + escalation triggers. Not legal advice — for internal use to speed up redlines and surface hard asks to legal/ops.

QUICK OBJECTIVE:
- Preserve ability to serve model inference on customer data without taking ownership of customer inputs/outputs.
- Limit indemnity and consequential exposure tied to model outputs.
- Ensure auditability and key custody options for regulated customers.
- Keep termination/transition simple: data export + KV cache wipe + runbook.

PRIORITY CLAUSES TO WATCH (ranked):
1) Data ownership & output rights — customers often try to force assignment of model outputs. Watch for language that assigns IP for any derivative output.
2) Indemnity for model outputs — never accept broad warranty that outputs are "accurate" or "fit for purpose."
3) Confidentiality scope & exceptions for aggregated telemetry — need narrow carve-outs for telemetry/metrics and safety monitoring.
4) Subprocessors / model providers / 3rd-party models — explicit right to use open/third-party models and to route to fallback models.
5) KMS / key custody / BYOK — clarify if Redwood holds keys or customer, and which keys protect what (control plane vs data plane).
6) SLA / credits calculus tied to multi-tenant hosting — define acceptable credit caps and exclusion events (training spikes, downstream infra).
7) Termination: data return/wipe, KV cache persistence, model artifacts — make timelines practical (30–60 days) and require authenticated request for export.

NOTES BY CLAUSE (storyboard style):
- Data ownership & outputs:
  Scenario: Large legal dept wants "all outputs produced by the Service" assigned to customer to avoid third-party claims.
  Risk: Broad assignment could block Redwood from using derivative telemetry to improve models or force thorny IP mapping.
  Seed redline: "Customer retains ownership of Customer Data. Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, revocable license to process Customer Data to provide the Service and for safety/telemetry purposes, subject to deletion obligations on termination."
  Tactical talking points: "We need the license to operate and to maintain service quality; it's limited to processing and safety improvements and does not transfer ownership."
  Fallback compromise: Accept customer ownership of raw inputs and outputs used within their account; Redwood keeps aggregated, anonymized metrics and derivative model improvements.
  Escalation trigger: Customer insists on assignment or 'work product' language that includes model weights or telemetry — escalate to Priya (Legal).

- Indemnity / representations:
  Scenario: Customer wants indemnity for any claim arising from outputs (including IP infringement).
  Risk: Models hallucinate; indemnity would expose Redwood to open-ended risk.
  Seed redline: "Redwood disclaims any warranty regarding factual accuracy of generated outputs. Redwood will indemnify Customer only for breaches of Redwood's obligations (security breach, unauthorized data disclosure)."
  Negotiation script: "We can accept indemnity for material breaches of our security obligations or willful misconduct, not for user-generated content or downstream use decisions."
  Fallback: Mutual, limited indemnity; cap at fees paid in 12 months; carve out direct infringement only for provided training/copyrighted materials which Redwood knowingly ingested.

- Confidentiality / telemetry:
  Scenario: Customer wants to prohibit any use of logs/telemetry that include derivative outputs.
  Risk: prevents monitoring safety regressions and unit economics improvements.
  Seed redline: "Redwood may collect and use aggregated, anonymized telemetry and usage metrics for service improvement; raw Customer Data remains confidential and will not be used to train models without explicit agreement."
  Tactic: Offer stronger anonymization guarantees and an audit log of what telemetry is ingested.

- Subprocessors / 3rd-party models:
  Scenario: Customer requires prior notice and opt-in for every subprocessor/model used.
  Risk: Operationally impossible — runtime may switch model variant for latency/reliability.
  Seed redline: "Redwood may engage subprocessors and model vendors; Redwood will publish a current list and provide reasonable notice for material changes. For emergency routing to compatible model variants, Redwood will notify post-facto if timely notice would harm availability."
  Negotiation tip: Offer monthly digest of model changes and an SLA-backed compatibility guarantee.

- KMS & BYOK:
  Scenario: Customer wants Redwood to hold all keys but still demands full control.
  Risk: key custody increases compliance burden and attack surface; BYOK preferred for regulated customers.
  Seed redline: "Customers may enable BYOK for data-at-rest encryption; Redwood will operate with customer-managed keys where feasible. Control plane keys used for orchestration remain Redwood-managed. Specifics to be scoped in SOW for private deployments."
  Compromise: Redwood offers HSM-backed key store with attestation reports for enterprise.

- Termination & migration:
  Scenario: Customer asks for six months to extract data and wants to keep cached prefixes that contain user prompts.
  Risk: KV cache could contain PII or customer secrets.
  Seed redline: "On termination Redwood will provide a machine-readable export of Customer Data within 30 days on authenticated request and will permanently delete KV caches and ephemeral logs within 30 days unless otherwise agreed."
  Talking point: "Deletion of KV cache reduces risk of leakage and aligns with our standard security posture; we can provide export first, then delete."

SCRIPTS: quick lines to use in calls
- "We operate on a limited license model so we can maintain service availability and continue to provide updates; ownership assignment would block that."
- "We can accept narrow indemnity for security incidents caused by Redwood, but not for outputs that are user-generated or inherently probabilistic."
- "For high-compliance customers, we offer BYOK and on-prem/private deployments under a separate SOW."

REDLINE SEEDS (copy/paste friendly):
- Ownership: "Customer Data: all data supplied by Customer. Redwood retains rights to aggregated, anonymized telemetry and derivative model improvements not attributable to Customer Data."
- Warranty disclaimer: "Service is provided \"AS IS\" for informational purposes; Redwood disclaims warranties of merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, and accuracy of generated outputs."
- Indemnity limit: "Each party's aggregate liability shall not exceed the fees paid by Customer to Redwood in the prior twelve (12) months; no party shall be liable for lost profits or consequential damages."

ESCALATION MATRIX (who to loop in):
- Legal: Priya Nair (contracts lead) — escalate for IP assignment, broad indemnities, export control issues.
- Security/Compliance: Mateo Ruiz — escalate on BYOK, key custody, audit requests, breach language.
- Product/Serving: Daniel Kim — escalate if customer demands runtime routing prohibitions or blocks telemetry collection.
- Sales/AE: Jordan Lee — coordinate commercial trade-offs and timeline.

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs:
- If a customer requires model training exclusion (no use of outputs to improve models), what exact language do we offer that still allows safety fixes? Action: ask Applied ML for "safety-only telemetry" definition. (Assigned: Miguel)
- Standard SLA credit cap — confirm with Finance if 6x monthly fee or 12x is acceptable as hard cap. (Assigned: Lina)
- Prepare short BYOK one-pager for AE — include attestation and HSM offering. (Assigned: Mateo)

NOTES TO SELF:
- Keep this short version in AE playbook.
- Build a snippet library in GH/GDrive with cut/paste seeds for each clause.
- When a customer claims outputs are their "work product," ask for concrete examples and use case before escalating.

END.
